measurements.name: who-flunet-activity-exceedance
measurements.grain: country x ISO week (ORIGIN_SOURCE streams summed)
measurements.systematic_rule: target country-year has >= 4 specimen-bearing weeks and >= 50% of them report INF_NEGATIVE >= 1; country-years judged systematic: 1258/3349
measurements.clustered_events_note: distinct_events counts country-years of the target week carrying at least one positive - positives arrive in seasonal clusters, so this is the effective sample size figure, per the candidate record

trap_acceptance.note: the discovery session measured 931/931 positive here; the pre-rule rate reproduces that uniform result, and the rule is judged by how few of those rows survive it

reference_baselines.note: stdlib rank AUC measured at construction on the written rows; scores are prediction-time-safe single features

measurements.crosscheck_hint: the built France 2024-25 positivity curve (summary.france_fixture) is the same series the publisher's FluNet chart app draws (worldhealthorg.shinyapps.io/flunetchart); the fixture asserts its peak and off-season levels from the source

source.name: WHO FluNet - Global Influenza Programme (World Health Organization, Geneva)
source.api: https://xmart-api-public.who.int/FLUMART/VIW_FNT?$format=csv (anonymous, no key, one request returns the full table)
source.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO (WHO copyright policy; NC/SA carried through). Derived research dataset - not a WHO official product.

licence_evidence.note: WHO copyright policy, read 2026-10-20 via search snippet of https://www.who.int/about/policies/publishing/copyright: 'Permission from WHO is not required for the use of WHO materials issued under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Intergovernmental Organization (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO) licence.' The licence 'allows users to freely copy, reproduce, reprint, distribute, translate and adapt the work for non-commercial purposes, provided WHO is acknowledged as the source'. Attribution form: '[Title]. [Place of publication]: World Health Organization; [Year]. Licence: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO.'

WHO dataset terms at data.who.int, read 2026-10-20 via search snippet of https://data.who.int/about/data/terms-and-conditions: 'Unless specifically indicated otherwise, these Datasets are provided to you under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0)' with mandatory citation per dataset metadata and a no-emblem clause. The FluNet tool page itself states no dataset-specific licence, so the general WHO posture (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO) is the conservative reading for this source; either way the terms permit redistribution of derived rows for non-commercial research with attribution, and any NC/SA conditions carry through unchanged.

baseline.purpose: one baseline through the runner's existing training and validation contract, on the accepted WHO FluNet country-week exceedance artifact

artifact.name: who-flunet-activity-exceedance
artifact.label_rule: target week (W+4) positivity INF_ALL/(INF_ALL+INF_NEGATIVE) > 0.10, denominator >= 50 and systematic negative reporting in the target country-year

baseline.scope: baseline only, through the runner's own contract. No agent or harness comparison was run, and none is implied.

rules: Code and documentation: MIT by default.
Our rights in a derived compilation: CC0-1.0 by default.
The source's own terms are preserved and never relicensed; the compilation dedication covers only our contribution.

Each dataset must use terms compatible with its sources. CC0 is NOT a blanket override of upstream terms: attribution, share-alike and non-commercial requirements from a source are carried through unchanged.
A source whose licence terms cannot be read is not published at all.
The chosen terms are declared per dataset in candidates/<id>/license.json and recorded in the release manifest, so the manifest cannot drift from the decision.
